prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B005 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 files show no disagreement about merit or maturity. The chain from proglucagon processing and the incretin effect, through the active truncated peptide and receptor biology, to long-acting agonists with large randomized outcome-trial benefit in glycaemia, weight, and cardiovascular and renal disease, is complete and independently replicated. The only open question is the third name, and that is a question about what the prize is for. A citation anchored on the physiology and active form of the hormone is the most defensible reading of a discovery prize. Holst supplies native human physiology, Drucker the receptor and tissue biology and its translation, and Mojsov the identification and synthesis of the active form on which the later analogue work depended. The citation still names incretin-based treatment, so the clinical outcome is acknowledged without making the prize an award for a product.
statement.case_against: The weakness I cannot remove is Mojsov's weight relative to Habener and others outside the credited names. I have no document in this packet that settles it, and several of us, myself included, are working partly from recollection. A Mojsov trio therefore adopts a contested priority claim, while a Knudsen trio adopts a framing in which the prize rewards drug development, which the committee has done sparingly. Either choice leaves a person with a real claim uncredited, and a discovery-only citation may look incomplete to a public that associates GLP-1 with liraglutide and semaglutide. I also note that all six of us ranked this first at the opening, so the committee should check that the unanimity reflects the evidence and not a shared well-known story.

responses.point: Linnarsson prefers Drucker, Holst and Knudsen, argues that Knudsen's acylation-based design is an original contribution and not routine optimisation, and says a citation spanning physiology and development is internally coherent.
responses.response: The acylation design is a real molecular invention and I do not call it routine. It is the step that made a once-weekly drug possible. My disagreement is about what the third seat records. Under a three-person cap, choosing Knudsen leaves the identification of the active peptide uncredited, and that identification is upstream of every analogue, including hers. I would accept your trio, as I said in round 1, if the committee concludes that Mojsov's priority cannot be defended. I have not reached that conclusion, because the dispute is about relative weight and not about whether the contribution happened. What would move me is a documented primary-source account showing that the active-form identification was substantially made by someone outside the credited names. Without that, I keep Mojsov.

responses.point: Sandberg keeps Knudsen because the therapeutic half of the citation would otherwise have no named contributor, but says she could move to a Mojsov trio if the citation were narrowed to physiology and peptide identification.
responses.response: That condition is what I propose, and I think it answers the chair's question. My citation is limited to the physiology of GLP-1 and its active form, and it names incretin-based treatment as the consequence and not as a credited achievement. I accept that this leaves the drug design unnamed. I think that is the lesser cost, since the therapeutic arc is stated in the citation and in the prize announcement, and the three-person cap forces one seat to carry one claim. If you can move to the Mojsov trio on those terms, the committee would have a five-to-one position with the remaining dissent resting on a single principled point. If you cannot, I would still prefer to say so openly in the vote and not blur the two configurations.

responses.point: Svenningsson prefers Mojsov to Knudsen because the Nobel tradition in this category rewards the discovery that opened the field, and asks that conduct questions not drive attribution without verified facts.
responses.response: I agree on the tradition and on the principle. Two clarifications. On Sabatini (B047), I raised a conduct concern in round 1 without putting verified facts on record, and I should not have left it ambiguous. I have no verified facts to add, so it should be set aside and play no part in any member's count. If it matters to the committee, it needs documented evidence and not a remark from me. B047 is not in my final configuration, so this does not change my position. My final position contains only B005, with B021 and B006 as alternatives.

responses.point: Perlmann ranks B006 second as a clean two-person mechanistic prize, but accepts that its disease link is indirect and that it is a later-year candidate or a second prize part.
responses.response: I agree with your assessment of Mori and Walter: no priority dispute, a mechanism confirmed over three decades. That is why it remains one of my two alternatives, and I take your point that it is the strongest fallback if the Mojsov and Knudsen question is judged unresolvable. I would still put it behind B005 on the medical mandate, because the delivered clinical benefit for GLP-1 is so much larger. On the chair's two-part question, you note correctly that B005 uses all three names, so adding B006 would require removing a B005 laureate. I would not pay that cost, because removing Mojsov or Holst to make room would damage the stronger part to improve the weaker one.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active peptide is substantial enough relative to Habener and others to justify a seat, which I cannot verify from the packet.
Whether the committee believes a discovery-only citation will be seen as incomplete without the drug designer, which is a judgement about the prize and not about the science.
Whether the Eshhar attribution gap for B021 can be resolved, which decides whether B021 is a serious alternative this year or a later-year candidate.
Whether the autoimmunity extension of CAR-T and the long-term toxicity record will mature enough to change my view of B021 in a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no documented involvement with any credited individual on B005, B021 or B006. My research is in autoimmunity, and CAR-T in autoimmunity (B021) is adjacent to my field, but I have no recorded tie to June, Sadelain or Rosenberg. My Bergen group-leader affiliation and past co-authors (Kuchroo, Sonesson) do not connect to any shortlisted candidate. I request no recusal.
